questions.q: Which operator does this course use for 'not equal to', and why?
options: <> — it's the ANSI SQL standard form
!= — it's the only form T-SQL supports
questions.explain: T-SQL supports both <> and !=, but <> is the ANSI standard, which is why this course uses it consistently.
WHERE ListPrice >= 500 includes products priced at exactly 500 as well as above it.

questions.q: How do dates compare using these operators?
options: Dates must be converted to strings first
Dates cannot be compared with these operators
The same way numbers do — earlier dates are 'less than' later ones
questions.explain: WHERE OrderDate > '2013-01-01' returns rows with a date later than January 1, 2013 — same logic as numeric comparison.

questions.q: Can a comparison operator be used against an expression, not just a bare column?
options: No, only a single column name is allowed
questions.explain: Comparisons evaluate against any valid expression, including calculations combining multiple columns.

questions.q: How many comparison operators does this lesson cover?
options: Four, since <> and != count as separate operators
questions.explain: AND/OR are logical operators covered in Lesson 13, not comparison operators.
